title.narrative: Multi Purpose Cash Assistance and Health services for IDP and famine response

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtThrough this project, IRC/SGR will work in Reif Ashargi county in R1. Reif Ashargi, having become accessible recently, displays the negative impact of being cut off and being insecure for the past years. The county lacks access to basic services infrastructure including that of health. ltbrgtSince the outbreak of conflict in Sudan, Reif Ashargi, like other parts of R1, has seen an IDP influx. Today, Reif Ashargi hosts 19.8% of all IDPs in R1 and is the county with maximum number of IDPs (based on Sudan Relief and Rehabilitation Agency 30th May 2024 update). ltbrgtThe failed 2023 harvest, locust infestation and sharp increase in prices of all supplies including food has created a situation of acute food insecurity in R1. Reif Ashargi too is facing acute food insecurity with it 60% population of the county being classified under IPC 3+ till February 2025. ltbrgtIRC/SGR will, through this project, provide access to essential primary health care in underserved communities in Reif Ashergi. The project is estimated to serve 19,292 people directly and 7,502 indirectly by providing Primary health care services, emergency response to disease outbreaks, essential obstetric care by supporting Department of Health with medicines, medical supplies, training, and rehabilitation for 3 health facilities in Reif Ashargi. The 3 health facilities have been selected in close coordination with Department of Health. ltbrgt ltbrgtIn this project, the IRC and SGR will provide 2,000 socio-economically vulnerable households (HHs) (12,000 individuals) with three rounds of unconditional multipurpose cash assistance (MPCA) in Reif Ashargi county. 1500 HHs among these (9000 individuals) will be IDPs and 500 HHs (3000 individuals) will be from host communities. This unrestricted cash assistance aims to meet the basic lifesaving needs of the vulnerablenbsp households by enabling them to purchase food/ non-food items in local markets. Despite the challenges, markets are functioning and are providing populations with basic needs. Given operational challenges in cash assistance, the IRC’s approach will be flexible and incorporate different delivery methods, including back-up financial service providers, alternate ways of assessing cash liquidity, and the option of switching to vouchers (specifically, e-vouchers) accessing the IRC’s existing service agreements with various service providers who operate in Sudan, and SGR’s deep knowledge of local markets which will include continued price and availability monitoring before, during, and after implementation.nbsp ltbrgtAs a part of SGR's strategy in this region, IRC will contribute by bringing its global technical expertise in CVA, MPCA, and experience implementing cash in Sudan, including in other areas of South Kordofan. IRC’s Cash Advisors will support the project including with staff training, developing tools and systems needed and providing oversight and guidance for quality control , risk identification and mitigations (including aid diversion, community and household level tensions and violence, other conflict sensitivity components, and negative market impact), during the entire program cycle. IRC’s tools IRC’s existing contracts with financial Service Providers and distribution software companies used in other areas of Sudan (i.e., RedRose, Genius Tags, etc.), will be used for this project. IRC will bring in its ability to implement both unrestricted cash or voucher programming as needed. ltbrgtWith IRC’s support outlined above, SGR will implement the programme bringing its context specific expertise and experience in designing and implementing community-based project in hard to reach locations of R1 and its experienced implementation teams who are trusted in target communities and already have exposure to distribution-based programs. ltbrgtThe project will be implemented in close coordination and collaboration with stakeholders including Authorities, other NGOs and peer agencies. ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgt ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtlt/pgtltpgtlt/pgt
